public_title: Why Your Heart Hurts on Goodbyes 💔
hook: You feel a physical ache when you say goodbye.

sections.title: Story
sections.narration: You feel a physical ache when you say goodbye. That pain is actually real biological distress. In 1999, researchers at the University of Texas measured brain activity during social rejection. They found the same regions lit up as physical injury. The result? Your brain treats a broken heart like a broken bone. So why do we assume feelings are just mental? It is a survival mechanism. In the 1600s, monks isolated themselves to protect their loyalty to the church. They knew separation triggered intense withdrawal symptoms. Modern studies confirm this across cultures. About 50 percent of people report this physical sensation after a breakup. Your body interprets loss as a threat to survival. So next time you feel that heavy chest pain after a farewell, remember your body is processing real danger. You feel a physical ache when you say goodbye.

claims.claim: Social rejection activates the same brain regions as physical pain
Isolation practices in religious orders were used to manage social threat responses
